subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 09, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 09, 2026

Development Updates: Over the past few days the team synchronized the newsletter, archive, and wiki guides to keep documentation current. This effort ensures that newcomers and veterans alike have access to the latest information about installation and usage. The sync was completed on September 8th and September 7th, reflecting our commitment to timely knowledge sharing.

Development Updates: Continuous integration improvements were made to the immutable build pipeline, including passing the -R flag to gh release create to avoid unnecessary checkouts. Additionally, a block‑scalar indentation issue in release.yml was fixed, restoring workflow validation. These changes streamline the release process and reduce potential errors for contributors.

Development Updates: The Xlibre spin received a missing dependency, with Firefox‑ublock‑origin added to the build to enhance ad‑blocking out of the box. A chore to re‑trigger the GitLab mirror resolved a deploy‑key hiccup, keeping our mirrors in sync. Shellcheck was also explicitly enabled on top‑level scripts to catch potential bugs early.

Community News: Jellyfin 12.0 has been released, bringing a refreshed user interface, improved transcoding performance, and better support for HDR content. Media enthusiasts in our community can now enjoy a more robust personal streaming server. The update is available through the standard repositories and is recommended for all existing installations.

Community News: Security updates have been issued by AlmaLinux and Debian, covering packages such as expat, git‑lf​s, grafana‑pcp, kernel‑rt, python3.14‑cryptography, redis, skopeo, xmlrpc‑c, and jbig2dec. Users are encouraged to apply these patches promptly to maintain system integrity. The AcreetionOS team has already incorporated the relevant fixes into our rolling release channel.

Community News: Activity on our Discord and GitLab servers remains vibrant, with members sharing tips on customizing the Cinnamon desktop and troubleshooting hardware compatibility. Recent contributions include new themes for the Xlibre spin and improvements to the Calamares installer configuration. This collaborative spirit keeps the project moving forward and welcoming to newcomers.

Tips & Highlights: When writing a new AcreetionOS image to USB, consider using the AcreetionMediaWriter tool, which works across Windows, macOS, and Linux. It simplifies the process by handling partitioning and verification automatically, reducing the chance of boot failures. A step‑by‑step guide is available on our wiki for those who prefer a manual approach.

Tips & Highlights: One of the core strengths of AcreetionOS is its commitment to privacy: the distribution includes no telemetry, and repository sovereignty ensures that users retain full control over their software sources. This design aligns with the principles of a user‑centric, transparent operating system. Regular audits of our build pipelines help maintain this guarantee.

Tips & Highlights: We invite everyone to join the conversation on Discord, report bugs on GitLab, or contribute documentation and code. Upcoming community events include a virtual showcase of user desktops scheduled for later this month and a beginner‑friendly workshop on kernel compilation. Your participation helps shape the future of AcreetionOS.
